written.myAnswer: Division of labour is the specialization of different cells or parts to perform specific tasks. In multicellular organisms, muscle cells contract to produce movement, nerve cells transmit impulses, and red blood cells carry oxygen.

Cell specialization (differentiation) is the development of cells with structures and features suited to particular functions. For example, mesophyll cells carry out photosynthesis, neurons transmit nerve impulses, and red blood cells carry oxygen.
Mitochondrial dysfunction or absence reduces the cell’s energy supply, so energy-dependent organelles may function less effectively, disrupting cell activities and survival.
